primitives.name: Persistent Skill Embedding
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model SAIL: (1) Participant-specific persistent embedding z_s ∈ R^d, learnable, shared across all trajectories of a participant (init N(0,0.1)); at test time model parameters (g_φ, q_θ, h_ψ) frozen, only z_s optimized.
primitives.assumptions: Embedding is stable across sessions, invariant to trial noise, and captures persistent behavioral traits.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When model parameters are frozen, z_s becomes the only learnable variable during inference.

layer2.mapping: z_s maps to a latent space where individual skill profiles are encoded as fixed vectors across time and context.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of SAIL lies in decomposing human skill into persistent, interpretable components through latent variable modeling. The persistent skill embedding z_s acts as a compressed, context-invariant descriptor of an individual’s skill profile. It is learned once and reused across all behavioral trajectories of a participant. The novice-expert basis blending mechanism allows for flexible behavior prediction by interpolating between known extremes—this is mathematically modeled as a weighted average of expert and novice trajectory bases. The key innovation is in the counterfactual subskill swap, which forces each component of z_s to encode a specific subskill by replacing it with donor values and observing the resulting behavior change. This ensures disentanglement and interpretability. The auxiliary mutual information network q_θ enforces that z_s retains sufficient information about the observed behavior, preventing collapse. Together, these primitives form a robust framework for predictive modeling of human skill, grounded in behavioral data rather than static features. Failure modes include overfitting due to insufficient data, poor generalization when expert/novice bases are misaligned, or collapse of z_s if mutual information constraints are too weak.
